newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peugeot seen taking control of Argentina's Sevel.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot seen taking control of Argentina's Sevel.

text.p: French carmaker Peugeot will take control of its Sevel affiliate which manufactures its autos in Argentina, Sevel's parent company was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
Mauricio Macri, chief of the SOCMA group controlling Sevel, told the Clarin newspaper that the French carmaker would inject new capital to take control of Sevel.

"Peugeot will invest in Sevel by injecting new capital, not buying existing shares, and therefore in a period of time to be determined it will end buying the share control," Macri said according to the daily Clarin. He did not elaborate on the capital injection.
"SOCMA will become a minor investor, something new for us, as we had always had the control and management of our companies.
"Only global firms can keep on thriving by getting models and autoparts from their different companies around the world and with the backing of international financial institutions," Macri said.
"That is what Fiat did. They chose to build their own plant in Cordoba (Argentine province) to make their models Palio and Siena," Macri said.
Fiat launched in April the Siena made in Cordoba for the world markets, and started building there the Palio. Between 1992 and July 1996 Fiat cars in Argentina were made by Sevel.

In March Sevel announced for 1996 a net gain of $21.4 million that included an extraordinary loss of $17.8 million. In 1995 it had a $127 million net loss that included an extraordinary loss of $83 million. At December 1996 its net worth stood at $387 million.
